name: route_toggle
description: One thousand route toggles between PC1 and PC2 with no lost, duplicated or misrouted event, and no key left held across a switch. This is the product's whole purpose, so it gets the largest sample count.
requires: U1 with a keyboard and a mouse attached
PC1 and PC2 both logged in and observing
on_this_rig: On this bench this scenario decides none of its own three questions. A route change is only observable as an event arriving at the other computer, and nothing here watches PC1 or PC2, so all_toggles_took_effect, no_misrouted_event and no_stuck_keys are all recorded as unmeasured. The runner also does not perform the write_config step, so the toggle binding has to be in the configuration already or the tap does nothing - which changes no verdict here, because none of the toggle checks is decided either way. What a run does decide is the three latency and stall checks, over whatever input flowed between the two phases. Run it for those; do not read a partial verdict here as 1000 toggles verified.

steps.note: one profile, Button 3 bound to TOGGLE_MOUSE_ROUTE

checks.no_misrouted_event: no injected event arrived on the computer it was not routed to
checks.no_stuck_keys: no key remained held across any switch
checks.no_gap_over_50ms: no observed pause longer than 50 ms
